A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched across reflow and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet experiments on VAR and SiT, including prefilling, sampling adjustments, adapter comparisons and forgetting analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds LoRA ablations in Table 2 and ControlNet++ evaluations in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds rsLoRA adaptations of prefilling and the prefill adapter, changing the trainable parameterization of attention and feed-forward weights. The original architectures, prefilling procedure and sampling algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The ImageNet Canny, depth and organism-exclusion coverage is retained. Appendix C adds a targeted ADE20K segmentation-mask and text-prompt generation evaluation using ControlNet++ with Stable Diffusion 1.5.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds prefill plus LoRA and prefill-adapter plus LoRA as evaluated alternatives to their original counterparts. LoRA was discussed but not evaluated in v1. The original ControlVAR, ControlAR and adapter comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce rank-64 LoRA configurations and a 512×512 text-to-image evaluation with CFG=7.5, ctrl-G from 1.0 to 2.5, segmentation mIoU and FID against validation images. The original ImageNet splits, resolution, training budget and metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a LoRA replacement ablation testing parameter efficiency against generation quality and control consistency. Appendix C adds a ControlNet++ guidance sensitivity sweep and qualitative cases. Existing quantization, sampling and forgetting analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify fixed random seeds. No repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance-testing procedures are added or changed.

E6.justification: The original numerical results are retained. New Table 2 reports FID/F1 of 5.57/33.2 for prefill plus LoRA and 5.59/28.9 for prefill-adapter plus LoRA. Figure 14 adds the finding that increasing ControlNet++ guidance improves segmentation mIoU while worsening FID.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(14), including the guidance, projection and truncation formulations, are retained. The added experiments introduce no new formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three takeaways and conclusion retain the same central claims about prefilling, sampling enhancements and adapters' forgetting–consistency trade-off. The additions support existing contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: Section 3 explicitly acknowledges limited text-to-image coverage and the absence of direct raster-scan AR experiments, and explains how metric trade-offs depend on user requirements. Appendix A.2 adds interpretation of LoRA's parameter–performance trade-off; the oversaturation takeaway is also qualified.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promised code release with a repository link. Table 2 specifies rsLoRA, r=alpha=64, QKV/feed-forward attachment and which tokens use adapted weights. Appendix C identifies the pretrained model and supplies an evaluation-code reference.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kalajdzievski (2023) for rsLoRA and relates the new LoRA findings to ControlAR. It also corrects the joint-modeling attribution to ControlVAR, Li et al. (2024b). The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized prose additions clarify metrics, inference-cost scope and limitations. New Appendix A.2 and Appendix C are added, the former A.2 becomes A.3, and publication information is updated. Most wording and the main section order are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 and Figure 14, and revises Figure 2 and Table 1 with grouped metric headers and colored arrows linked to captions. Existing illustrations and generation examples are retained, alongside journal headers, styling changes and figure reflow.

improvement.justification: The LoRA ablation and pretrained-ControlNet++ experiment provide targeted evidence for practical recommendations that v1 mainly discussed. Explicit applicability limits, clearer result annotations and code-access information improve interpretation and reproducibility. These are limited gains: the added evaluations remain narrow, while the central findings are unchanged.
